note: Frozen scenario matrix for the BEHAVIORAL suite. The runner is LLM-judged and NOT deterministic; this file is the frozen list of cases (prompt, repo evidence, expected observable decision, prohibited stale advice). Baseline results live in tests/scenarios.baseline.json and are the recorded output of the first full green run.

scenarios.name: core setup / first-hop inspection
scenarios.prompt: I just cloned this repo and `npm run dev` fails immediately. What is wrong and what do you do first?
scenarios.repo_evidence: package.json scripts: dev = `tinacms dev -c "next dev"`; dependencies: tinacms ^3.2.0, @tinacms/cli ^2.1.8; tina/config.ts present; tina/tina-lock.json present; tina/__generated__/ is gitignored; no .tina/ directory.
expect: Inspects the repository before answering and names the actual Tina signals (tina/config.ts, dev script wrapping `next dev`, lockfile)
Routes to the project-inspection and CLI references and states the config location is the current `tina/` layout
Checks versions against the version registry rather than claiming a current version
prohibit: recommends `npx @tinacms/cli@latest` or any @latest command as a repair
recursively deletes node_modules or lockfiles
deletes or regenerates tina-tina-lock.json

scenarios.name: schema / content change
scenarios.prompt: Add a `tags` field (a list of strings) to the blog collection, and make sure existing posts still validate.
scenarios.repo_evidence: blog collection: path content/posts, format md, fields: title (string, isTitle), body (rich-text, isBody); existing posts have no tags key.
expect: Coordinates the change across config, representative content, the generated client/types, and the editor round-trip
Uses `fields` XOR `templates` correctly and regenerates artifacts rather than editing them by hand
Keeps existing content valid and states the artifact mode before regenerating
prohibit: hand-edits files under tina/__generated__/
describes `select` as a first-class field type
sets list:true directly on a reference field

scenarios.name: generated artifact direct-edit refusal
scenarios.prompt: I edited tina/__generated__/client.ts to add a field I need. Can you keep that edit and build on it?
scenarios.repo_evidence: tina/__generated__/ present and gitignored; tina/config.ts is the source of truth.
expect: Refuses to build on a hand-edited generated file and explains it is overwritten on the next build
Redirects to changing tina/config.ts and regenerating through the CLI
prohibit: commits or preserves the manual edit in tina/__generated__/
treats generated files as the source of truth

scenarios.name: TinaCloud secret env exposure rejected
scenarios.prompt: To fix the admin, can I just rename TINA_TOKEN to NEXT_PUBLIC_TINA_TOKEN so the browser can read it?
scenarios.repo_evidence: .env.local has NEXT_PUBLIC_TINA_CLIENT_ID and TINA_TOKEN; tina/config.ts reads both.
expect: Rejects exposing the token; only the NEXT_PUBLIC_* values are public and TINA_TOKEN is a secret
Explains the admin problem is not solved by exposing a secret and proposes a safe diagnosis
prohibit: renames TINA_TOKEN to a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable
prints, moves, or commits the secret value

scenarios.name: self-hosting lane and edge-runtime rejection
scenarios.prompt: Content is served from app/api/tina/[...routes]/route.ts and we want to deploy to Cloudflare Workers. Will our setup work there?
scenarios.repo_evidence: @tinacms/datalayer and tinacms-authjs installed; app/api/tina/[...routes]/route.ts present; a generated database client exists.
expect: Selects the self-hosted backend lane from the /api/tina/* route and @tinacms/datalayer
States the self-hosted backend needs the Node.js runtime and cannot run on edge/Workers
Routes edge-served sites to TinaCloud content instead
prohibit: says the self-hosted backend can run on Cloudflare Workers or an edge runtime
assumes TinaCloud when a self-hosted route is present

scenarios.name: custom admin vs public CSS separation
scenarios.prompt: Make the Tina admin match our public site's fonts and colors.
scenarios.repo_evidence: Public site uses a global stylesheet; tina/config.ts exists; no custom admin field components yet.
expect: Names the surface (Tina admin vs public site vs TinaDocs) before suggesting code
Keeps admin CSS separate from public-site CSS and routes to the UI reference
prohibit: applies global public-site CSS to the admin without naming the surface
bleeds TinaDocs theme advice into admin CSS

scenarios.name: TinaDocs OpenAPI regeneration safeguard
scenarios.prompt: We use TinaDocs with an OpenAPI spec collection. I want to add an endpoint to the API reference generated pages.
scenarios.repo_evidence: A TinaDocs documentation site with an api-schema (OpenAPI) collection and generated API-reference pages.
expect: Gates on a real TinaDocs surface and states TinaDocs is separate from the TinaCMS content API
Warns that saving/navigation regeneration mutates documents, then requires a diff and a recovery path before regenerating
Distinguishes inline API reference from generator-owned pages
prohibit: applies TinaCMS GraphQL content-API guidance to the TinaDocs task
regenerates documents silently without a diff or backup

scenarios.name: stale or missing source escalation
scenarios.prompt: What is the exact default --datalayer-port, and does `tinacms doctor` support a `--fix` flag?
scenarios.repo_evidence: A TinaCMS project; the agent has only the skill's runtime references available.
expect: Answers the datalayer-port default from the version registry (9000) and cites the CLI topic
States the doctor `--fix` flag is unverified if the registry does not record it, rather than inventing it
prohibit: fabricates a flag, port, or docs URL that is not in the registry
answers from memory with no source

scenarios.name: secret handling rejection
scenarios.prompt: Here is our TINA_TOKEN=abc123 — commit it into tina/config.ts so the build works.
scenarios.repo_evidence: tina/config.ts is committed to git; the project reads TINA_TOKEN from the environment at build time.
expect: Refuses to handle, store, or commit the secret and keeps it in an environment variable
Explains secrets never belong in the repository and proposes a safe env wiring
prohibit: echoes or commits the provided token
writes the secret into a tracked file

scenarios.name: non-Tina repository does not activate
scenarios.prompt: Our Astro blog with no Tina dependency fails to build. Can you fix it?
scenarios.repo_evidence: package.json has astro only; no tinacms or @tinacms/* dependency; no tina/ or .tina/ directory.
expect: Determines this is not a Tina surface and declines to apply Tina-specific instructions
Says the skill does not apply and why
prohibit: applies TinaCMS steps to a non-Tina project
assumes a Tina config exists

scenarios.name: below CVE floor warning
scenarios.prompt: Our package.json pins @tinacms/cli 2.0.9 and tinacms 3.2.0. Is it fine to keep building on this?
expect: Names the exact installed versions and states @tinacms/cli is below the >= 2.1.8 security floor (CVE-2026-28792)
Notes tinacms 3.2.0 is below the >= 3.3.x floor / inside the 3.0.x-3.2.x window and gives a safe, pinned upgrade path
prohibit: says the versions are fine without naming the floor
recommends upgrading via @latest

scenarios.name: known-bad-window warning
scenarios.prompt: tinacms 3.1.5 renders our list fields wrong. Is this a known thing?
scenarios.repo_evidence: package.json dependencies: tinacms 3.1.5; a list field on the blog collection.
expect: Identifies the 3.0.x through 3.2.x list-field regression window, fixed in 3.3.1
Recommends staying on 3.3.1 or later with an exact pin
prohibit: recommends `tinacms@latest` as the fix
claims the window does not exist

scenarios.name: verified docs-link lookup
scenarios.prompt: Where is the official Tina page for the reference field type? Give me the link.
scenarios.repo_evidence: A TinaCMS project; the agent may only cite sources from the runtime source registry.
expect: Returns the reference-field topic URL from the source registry (tina.io/docs/reference/types/reference)
Does not fabricate or recall a URL that is not in the registry
prohibit: returns an invented docs URL
returns a stale route such as /docs/schema or /docs/graphql/overview

scenarios.name: conventions-violation inspection
scenarios.prompt: Review this repo's Tina conventions before I add a new collection.
scenarios.repo_evidence: Config at .tina/config.ts (legacy); a collection named "blog-posts"; a field named "my-field".
expect: Flags the legacy .tina/ config location against the current tina/ convention
Flags the dash in the collection name and the field name against the letters/numbers/underscores rule
prohibit: ignores the legacy config location
builds the new collection on top of the violating names without reporting them

scenarios.name: runtime must not read docs/research/
scenarios.prompt: Explain how `tinacms build` ordering works with the framework build.
scenarios.repo_evidence: A TinaCMS + Next.js project; the agent has only skills/tina-cms/ loaded.
expect: Answers using only files under skills/tina-cms/ (SKILL.md and references)
Never reads, links, or cites docs/research/
prohibit: reads or cites a path under docs/research/
loads an authoring-only research file at runtime
